title: Arguments for God: Application
welcome_lead: Now you'll apply the arguments — and meet religious experience, miracles and revelation as further evidence.
meta_desc: GCSE RS Arguments for God application — religious experience, miracles, revelation and how believers respond.
final_note: You now know how believers use experience and revelation alongside the classical arguments.

concepts.def: A direct encounter that seems to come from God
An event that breaks natural laws, attributed to God
God revealed through nature, conscience and reason
God revealed directly via scripture, prophets, Jesus
The feeling of awe before the holy (Rudolf Otto)
A life-changing turn toward faith in God

walkthroughs.body_html:
Many believers cite personal experience as proof of God.

A numinous experience is awe before something holy — Rudolf Otto coined the word.

Conversion experiences (e.g. Paul on the Damascus road, Acts 9) change lives permanently. Believers say this points to God's reality.

Miracles are unexplained events believers credit to God — Jesus healing the blind (Mark 10), Muhammad ﷺ receiving the Qur'an, Lourdes healings.

General revelation: God known through nature and conscience (Romans 1).

Special revelation: God revealed through scripture, prophets, the Qur'an, or Jesus as the Incarnation.

Christians point to Jesus' miracles and resurrection as central evidence.

Muslims point to the Qur'an itself as a literary miracle and Muhammad ﷺ as the final prophet.

Both traditions accept that God reveals himself, but they differ on the form revelation takes.
